nodes.name: Coprecipitation synthesis of dicarboxylate-intercalated NiFe LDHs
nodes.procedure: Dicarboxylic acids (suberic acid (COOH)(CH2)6(COOH), adipic acid (COOH)(CH2)4(COOH) and succinic acid (COOH)(CH2)2(COOH)) intercalated NiFe LDHs were synthesized by using a similar coprecipitation method mentioned in our previous work [21]. Instead of 0.015 mol of dicarboxylic acid [20], here 0.225 mol suberic acid, adipic acid, or succinic acid were dissolved in NaOH solution and were then slowly added to a solution containing ferric nitrate (nonahydrate, Fe(NO3)3·9H2O) and nickel nitrate (hexahydrate, Ni(NO3)2·6H2O) (molar ratio of 3:1), forming a suspension. The resulting suspensions were then aged at 85°C under Ar protection for 4 days with magnetic stirring after the pH of the suspensions were tuned to around 7 by adding NaOH solution. The final products were centrifuged and washed with DI water and then the obtained solids were dried in air at 60°C. The obtained LDH samples were designated as NiFe LDH Sub for suberic acid intercalated NiFe LDH, NiFe LDH Adp for adipic acid intercalated NiFe LDH and NiFe LDH Suc for succinic acid intercalated NiFe LDH.

nodes.description: Chronopotentiometry stability test at 1.682-1.684 V vs RHE
nodes.source_text: The stability of each sample was evaluated by chronoamperometry performed at 1.682–1.684 V vs RHE (Fig. 4d). All the NiFe LDHs intercalated with dicarboxylate anions showed great OER stability with no activity decay in 24 h. They all generated higher current densities than that of RuO₂ at this potential... NiFe LDH Seb and NiFe LDH Sub also showed a small increase in current density over time.

nodes.characterization_summary: (003) diffraction peaks at different low-angle positions indicate varying interlayer spacings: NiFe LDH Seb 14.3 Å, NiFe LDH Sub 10.5 Å, NiFe LDH Adp 8.3 Å, NiFe LDH Suc 6.6 Å, NiFe LDH CO 2.9 Å. Peaks at 33.9° and 60° confirm LDH phase formation.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In Fig. 1a (powder XRD of each sample), the (003) diffraction peaks of each intercalated NiFe LDH sample can be clearly observed at different positions in the low angle range (Table 1)... Peaks at 33.9° and 60° can also be clearly observed in all patterns of NiFe LDHs, which are due to the diffractions of (012) and (110) planes of LDH

properties.description: X-ray Diffraction pattern of Intercalated NiFe LDHs on FTO before reaction

nodes.characterization_summary: C-H stretching bands at 2925 cm⁻¹ and 2852 cm⁻¹ confirm dicarboxylate intercalation in NiFe LDH Seb, Sub, Adp (absent in Suc due to short chains). Carbonyl vibrations at 1541 cm⁻¹ and 1409 cm⁻¹ present in intercalated LDHs, absent in NiFe LDH CO.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Two bands at 2925 cm⁻¹ and 2852 cm⁻¹ (Fig. 1c) which can be attributed to the stretching vibrations of methylene C–H bonds... Bands at 1541 cm⁻¹ and 1409 cm⁻¹ (Fig. 1d) in the intercalated NiFe LDHs can be attributed to the asymmetric and symmetric vibrations of carbonyl groups

nodes.characterization_summary: NiFe LDH Seb shows unique spherical morphology (85-105 nm); NiFe LDH Sub and Adp show conventional 2D platy morphology (~100 nm); NiFe LDH Suc shows monoliths of densely-packed ultrafine particles.
nodes.evidence_snippet: SEM (Fig. 2) and TEM (Fig. 3) images revealed that only NiFe LDH Seb was spherical (particle size 85-105 nm), while NiFe LDH Sub and NiFe LDH Adp both showed a conventional 2D platy morphology with particle sizes for both around 100 nm

nodes.characterization_summary: Confirms SEM morphologies: NiFe LDH Seb spherical (85-105 nm), NiFe LDH Sub/Adp platy (~100 nm), NiFe LDH Suc ultrafine particle aggregates. SAED confirms polycrystalline LDH phase with poor crystallinity.
nodes.evidence_snippet: SEM (Fig. 2) and TEM (Fig. 3) images revealed that only NiFe LDH Seb was spherical... In addition, selected area electron diffraction (SAED) (Fig. S2) also confirmed the formation of LDH phase in each sample

nodes.characterization_summary: BET surface areas: NiFe LDH Sub 9.588 m²/g, NiFe LDH Adp 8.13 m²/g (NiFe LDH CO higher than intercalated LDHs per Table S5).
nodes.evidence_snippet: The BET surface area of NiFe LDH CO was much larger than those of NiFe LDHs intercalated with different dicarboxylate anions (Table S5, isotherm shown in Fig. S8)

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni 2p binding energies: Seb/Adp/CO 855.7-855.9/873.6-873.9 eV, Sub/Suc slightly higher at 856.5-856.6/874.5 eV indicating higher Ni oxidation state. Fe 2p: Seb 711.3 eV (lower), others ~712.5-713 eV. Ni/Fe ratios: Seb 1.45, Sub 2.1, Adp 2.0, Suc 2.3.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Ni 2p core-binding energies (Fig. 6a) of NiFe LDH Seb, NiFe LDH Adp and NiFe LDH CO are 855.7–855.9 eV... The Ni/Fe ratio in NiFe LDH Seb detected by XPS was 1.45

nodes.characterization_summary: SAED confirms LDH phase formation and reveals all dicarboxylate intercalated NiFe LDHs are polycrystalline with relatively poor crystallinity.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In addition, selected area electron diffraction (SAED) (Fig. S2) also confirmed the formation of LDH phase in each sample. Besides, SAED also revealed that the dicarboxylic anions intercalated NiFe LDHs were all polycrystalline with relatively poor crystallinity.
